andro-rasanter-r42: Softer, forgiving rubber suited to the backhand, but it can feel mushy and may lack forehand power.
andro-rasanter-r47: Spinny, fairly hard backhand rubber preferred to G-1 or Rozena; blocking and the short game suffer.
butterfly-dignics-05: Fast, spinny and very durable for aggressive players; many find it too fast to control for blocks.
butterfly-dignics-09c: Tacky, very spinny and good in the short game, though the hard, fast feel is tricky on the backhand.
butterfly-fan-zhendong-alc: Fast carbon blade with real feedback, surprisingly controllable; some find it too stiff or direct.
butterfly-glayzer-09c: Slower, softer and more forgiving take on Dignics 09C; some find it mushy and the grip fades.
butterfly-harimoto-innerforce-alc: Forgiving carbon blade with a big sweet spot and dwell; some find it slower and softer than Viscaria.
butterfly-harimoto-innerforce-super-alc: Faster than the regular ALC yet stable and precise; beginners may struggle to activate it.
butterfly-innerforce-layer-alc: Controllable and fast at once for pushing and looping; a few find it muted or stiff at first.
butterfly-petr-korbel: All-wood blade fast for a 5-ply, with great feel; it is heavy, head-heavy and has a thin handle.
butterfly-primorac: All-wood control and consistency for years, but slower, so some want more power as they improve.
butterfly-timo-boll-alc: Fast carbon blade with power on loops and blocks; several find it unforgiving near the table.
butterfly-viscaria: Crisp, fast carbon-feel blade liked on the backhand; beginners find the low dwell hard to control.
dhs-fang-bo-b2x: Inner carbon blade that adds speed without losing touch, at strong value; a few find it hollow.
dhs-hurricane-3: Slow, very spinny rubber that forces full strokes; the hard sponge is demanding and the tack fades.
dhs-hurricane-3-neo: Spinny and linear, a favourite of loopers, but hard to control without full-body strokes.
dhs-hurricane-3-neo-national: Tacky with strong spin, usually boosted on the forehand; demanding, and the grip fades.
dhs-hurricane-301: Close to all-wood in feel with extra power and good value; the slim handle lets it down.
dhs-hurricane-8-80: Tacky backhand rubber for beginners and intermediates that needs no boosting; sheets run heavy.
dhs-power-g7: Great-value all-wood blade and a fine first one; the narrow handle and extra weight are minor gripes.
donic-baracuda: Grippy, high-throw rubber liked on the backhand for looping; a few find it dated or short on speed.
nittaku-acoustic: All-wood blade prized for feel and feedback that lasts for years; the thin handle irks some.
nittaku-acoustic-carbon-inner: More power and a bigger sweet spot than the all-wood Acoustic; one found it stiffer.
nittaku-fastarc-c-1: Softer, more forgiving take on G-1, popular on the backhand; a handful find it bouncy or mushy.
nittaku-fastarc-g-1: Controllable, durable and spinny with a linear feel; the bouncy arc is hard to control for some.
stiga-allround-classic: Soft, vibrant blade ideal for learning spin and blocking, though slow, and some outgrow it.
stiga-cybershape-carbon-cwt: Aggressive and fast with a large sweet spot and adjustable weights, though it feels hard and direct.
stiga-cybershape-wood: Good feel and a balance of speed and control.
stiga-infinity-vps-v: Wood blade with good speed and great control, fit for a first custom setup; a few found it too fast.
tibhar-evolution-mx-s: Spinny on either side, preferred to MX-P for control and lifespan; the hard sponge needs a big swing.
tibhar-hybrid-k3: Tacky, springy forehand rubber and a cheaper alternative to Dignics 09C; it wears out fast.
tibhar-quantum-x-pro: Safe, spin-insensitive rubber with good control, playing softer and somewhat slower.
tibhar-stratus-power-wood: All-wood blade with good control and feel that many keep for years, though the large head is heavy.
victas-curl-p1v: Pips rated very highly for chopping and defence; hard to control for some.
victas-triple-double-extra: Very spinny and fast, but the tackiness fades within weeks and it cannot be boosted.
yasaka-ma-lin-carbon: Fans like the control, grip and speed, especially inner carbon; others found it stiff, like a plank.
yasaka-ma-lin-extra-offensive: Five-ply all-wood offensive blade popular for penhold; the handle is short and thin.
yasaka-rakza-7: Controllable, spinny and durable, often recommended for beginners; some find it too bouncy at max.
yasaka-rakza-xx: Grippy and spinny, with a hard sponge that rewards strong players; several found it demanding.
yasaka-rakza-z: Tacky hybrid with strong spin and a good short game, though many call it heavy.
yasaka-sweden-classic: All-wood feel and control, not the fastest, which makes it a good blade for beginners.
yasaka-sweden-extra: Slow, soft and very controllable at a fair price, though several dislike the thin handle.
